title: Weaving Feminist Pedagogy Principles with International Student Experiences in Canadian College Economics Courses
text_snippet: Weaving Feminist Pedagogy Principles with International Student Experiences in Canadian College Economics Courses Feminist pedagogy, grounded in feminist theory and critical pedagogy, aims to problematize power inequalities and promote justice, thereby guiding our pedagogical practices. Educators in the field seek an equitable education that honours experiential knowledge while empowering and liberating marginalized groups. Traditionally, feminist scholars have focused on political goals; however, their application in peer-reviewed journals is sparse. This paper advocates actionable strategies for implementing feminist pedagogy, particularly in traditionally male-dominated fields such as economics. With an emphasis on adult learners in Canadian polytechnic economics courses, we begin with a literature review of feminist pedagogy in practice. This quantitative study then examines the effectiveness of feminist pedagogical techniques through the experiences of adult learners (N = 108), particularly international students, who comprised 92.5% of participants. The findings reveal three key themes: fostering community, sharing power between students and teachers, and promoting care, which align with the core principles of feminist pedagogy. title: Improving Entrepreneurship Education through a HOTS-Based Digital Assessment Tool Infused with Prophetic Values
text_snippet: Improving Entrepreneurship Education through a HOTS-Based Digital Assessment Tool Infused with Prophetic Values Entrepreneurship education requires assessments that develop higher-order thinking while encouraging ethical reflection. This study developed and evaluated a learning-oriented digital assessment tool integrating Higher-Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) with prophetic values of honesty, responsibility, transparency, and wisdom, operationalized as culturally situated expressions of virtue ethics within authentic entrepreneurship tasks and rubrics. Guided by the Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation (ADDIE) model, the study used a multiphase, mixed-methods research-and-development design involving 131 undergraduates: 30 pilot participants, 71 intervention participants, and 30 comparison participants. Quantitative data were examined using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, significance testing, and effect-size estimation; student reflections were analyzed thematically. Four experts produced an average content-validity score of 81.67%, and the instrument demonstrated strong internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = .874). title: English-Medium Instruction for University STEM Education in Hong Kong: The Lens of Language Teaching and Learning
text_snippet: English-Medium Instruction for University STEM Education in Hong Kong: The Lens of Language Teaching and Learning This book offers a timely and useful contribution to current discussions on English-medium instruction (EMI), STEM education, and language teaching in higher education. Although the book focuses on Hong Kong, its central concern is relevant to many multilingual university contexts: how students learn complex disciplinary knowledge through English, and how institutions can support them more effectively.

title: Trends and Innovations in the Development of Creative Thinking Skills in Education: A Comprehensive Analysis
text_snippet: Trends and Innovations in the Development of Creative Thinking Skills in Education: A Comprehensive Analysis This study aims to conceptually and technically review the literature on creative thinking skills (CTS) in education through bibliometric analysis. This study addresses several key research areas: descriptive features of retrieved empirical studies on CTS, annual scholarly production trends and thematic evolution of CTS, the most relevant and high-impact sources using Bradford's Law in CTS, the most cited articles on CTS, the most relevant countries for CTS research, and trending research themes for further investigation in the field of CTS. This study analyzed 641 articles from the Scopus database published between 2015 and 2025 using a systematic literature review and a bibliometric analysis approach. The main tools used in the analysis were VOSviewer and Biblioshiny. The results showed that CTS is an increasingly important research area in education, with scholarly output increasing steadily from 2015 to 2025. Key topics such as project-based learning, technology integration, and human-centred educational approaches dominate the research trends.
